messages.text: As for 1. and 2.) break the paradigm that endcaps need to start at barrel length, allow stepped muon endcaps and redraw the designs
I’ll update the candidate layouts to allow stepped muon endcaps, check their interfaces with the calorimeters and magnets, and regenerate the drawings for PR #6.

The revised endcaps will have a narrower section extending upstream inside the barrel, followed by a wider section beyond it. I’m placing the upstream fronts 0.15 m beyond the HCal for inner-solenoid options, and beyond the coil assembly for outer-solenoid options. These are provisional clearances; shielding, services and end-return structures still need allocations.

All six stepped layouts pass the envelope-intersection checks, and the drawings are regenerated. The retained 0.40 m aperture matters at the earlier front: an eta=3.5 straight ray enters the inner-solenoid endcap host at about |z|=6.62 m, rather than at its 6.35 m front. I’ve documented that limit.

The new drawings show the upstream steps, and the code no longer ties the endcap front to barrel length. Four new tests, the existing envelope and documentation tests, and the dashboard checks passed. I’m updating PR #6 with the drawings and revised summary; the remaining magnetic-performance review questions stay open.

Updated [PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6) with stepped endcaps for all six layouts and regenerated PNG/SVG drawings.

- Narrower endcap sections extend upstream inside the barrel, then widen downstream.
- Fronts start at **6.35 m** for inner-solenoid options and **6.95 m** for outer-solenoid options.
- DES-004, option cards, validation records and PR summary updated.
- All six overlap checks and **30 tests passed**; dashboard and logs validated.

Clearances and shared magnet/service space remain provisional. The baseline is unchanged.
